principle: Source reliability is evaluated per use. A strong identity source is not automatically strong evidence for a historical causal claim.

tiers.A: Primary scholarly dataset or peer-reviewed source with explicit provenance
tiers.B: Curated scholarly/reference infrastructure suitable for identity, place, bibliography or contextual metadata
tiers.C: Discovery/index source; candidate generation only until source review
tiers.R: Reference media; visual context only unless separately bound to evidence

sources.name: Database of Religious History
sources.claim_policy: Upstream coding remains attributed; NOEMA crosswalks do not convert coding into historical causation.

sources.name: D-PLACE
sources.claim_policy: Focal year is observation/reference metadata, not culture-origin date.

sources.name: Pulotu
sources.claim_policy: Accepted mappings are comparative coding, not proof of diffusion or ancestry of a belief.

sources.name: Seshat Global History Databank
sources.claim_policy: Ingest only with variable-level provenance and versioned snapshot.

sources.name: ARIADNE Research Infrastructure
sources.claim_policy: Discovery/context layer; interpretation requires underlying archaeological evidence.

sources.name: Crossref
sources.claim_policy: Metadata is never evidence. Candidates require source review.

sources.name: OpenAlex
sources.claim_policy: Discovery and bibliometric context only until primary source review.

sources.name: Pleiades
sources.claim_policy: Place linking only; not evidence for religious meaning.

sources.name: Wikidata
sources.claim_policy: Identity/linking layer, never sole scholarly evidence.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons
sources.claim_policy: Media is iconographic/reference context unless separately evidence-bound.

sources.name: Museum open-access/reference media
sources.claim_policy: Remote thumbnails may be blocked by provider CORP/CORS; NOEMA must not hotlink when embedding is disallowed.

preferred: museum open-access downloads mirrored only when license permits
NOEMA-generated explanatory illustrations clearly labeled as generated
avoid: generated reconstructions presented as historical evidence
